fix: Broadcom fixed it … More → The post VMware vCenter zero-day exploited for months before patch (CVE-2026-123890) appeared first on Help Net Security .
impact: A suspected China-nexus espionage group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) has been exploiting a VMware vCenter zero-day since at least early September, more than two months before Broadcom released a fix, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) revealed. The vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890) carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to obtain an administrator session on vCenter Server, which organizations use to manage their VMware servers and virtual machines.

fix: Security Teams Advised to Monitor Email Volumes** Fortra recommended that security teams monitor email volume per recipient against the normal baseline. Investigate bursts involving many unrelated senders, subscription wording and mailing-list headers. Security teams should also confirm the scope and duration directly with the email delivery provider.
impact: This email flood can interrupt activities like customer service and routine correspondence, as well as obscuring account alerts, payment notifications and other messages that may require attention. The mail bombing campaign has been followed by vishing calls in which contact is made by the threat actor through Teams. “In the calls, the threat actors are claiming to be representatives from Internal IT, providing the user both verbal and email instructions they claim will stop the flood, but in reality, attempting to compromise the user account, system, or both,” the researchers explained.

fix: BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of _KEV Catalog vulnerabilities_.

fix: If you run Expressway, update now, hunt for those indicators, and don’t assume a clean edge device means a clean network behind it. Cisco shipped a fix on 21 October, so this wasn’t a zero-day by the time it got used.
impact: The attackers started with two internet-facing Expressway boxes. _“The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices.” reads theadvisory by F6. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” _ The attackers used custom Python scripts to scan networks, find accessible SMB resources, connect to SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories. Their goal was to steal credentials and other sensitive information.
